summary: Go Grep has converged on the broad TS surface (same public tool name, core parameters, ripgrep-backed path, default head_limit, output modes, multiline flag, and many direct Execute tests), but it is not yet a full implementation match. The largest remaining gaps are in runtime lifecycle wiring, permission/ignore integration, exact model-facing output and structured result data, rg binary resolution/fallback semantics, cwd scoping, sorting/pagination order, strict input/coercion edge cases, timeout partial-result behavior, and test coverage. A focused verification command (`go test ./tools -run 'TestGrep' -count=1`) is currently blocked before Grep tests run by unrelated tools package compile errors in MCP files.

gaps.title: Read-permission and allowed-directory lifecycle is not wired for Grep
gaps.description: TS Grep participates in the central read permission lifecycle: it declares read-only/search behavior, derives a path with getPath, prepares a permission matcher from the pattern, validates path existence without probing UNC paths, and delegates to checkReadPermissionForTool. Go Grep is an Execute-only stateless tool. Allowed search directory helpers exist and direct tests can set them manually, but SetupRegistry/UpdateSessionContext do not populate the search allow-list, so production Grep path scoping is effectively disabled unless some other caller sets package-global state. Go also turns UNC paths into hard tool errors where TS routes them through read-permission ask behavior.

ts_evidence.note: TS declares concurrency/read-only/search classification, getPath, and preparePermissionMatcher.
TS validates existing paths, skips UNC stat to avoid credential leaks, and delegates permission checks to checkReadPermissionForTool.
checkReadPermissionForTool checks resolved paths and returns ask for UNC reads instead of performing filesystem access.

go_evidence.note: Go Tool exposes Name, Description, Schema, and Execute only; there is no Grep-specific permission hook equivalent.
UpdateSessionContext updates file tools and shell cwd, but not search allowed dirs for Glob/Grep.
SetupRegistry registers a bare &tools.GrepTool{} without injecting allowedDirs or permission context.
Allowed search dirs are package-global state and default to allowing every path when unset.
resolveGrepSearchPath enforces the package global allow-list and hard-errors on UNC paths, but that allow-list is not wired by registry setup.

gaps.impact: Security and lifecycle parity gap: Grep can search outside intended allowed directories in default runtime wiring, and UNC/read permission behavior differs from TS.

gaps.title: File-read deny rules and orphaned plugin-cache exclusions are not applied to Grep
gaps.description: TS Grep converts live file-read deny rules into negative ripgrep --glob filters and also excludes orphaned plugin cache directories before search execution. Go has file-read ignore helpers, but Grep's ripgrep path does not add those patterns, Grep's fallback file collection does not filter them, and the registry does not populate the global ignore/plugin exclusion state. This can expose denied paths in Grep results and can let denied/orphaned files consume head_limit slots.

ts_evidence.note: TS normalizes getFileReadIgnorePatterns from appState.toolPermissionContext and appends them as negative --glob filters.
TS appends orphaned plugin-cache exclusions as ripgrep glob exclusions.
Plugin cache exclusions are session-scoped, overlap-aware, and best-effort.

go_evidence.note: runGrepWithRipgrep builds --hidden, VCS, max-columns, mode, pattern, type, and user glob args, but no file-read deny or plugin-cache exclusions.
collectGrepFallbackFiles walks candidate files and applies only grepFallbackFileAllowed; it does not filter file-read ignored paths.
grepFallbackFileAllowed only checks type and glob filters.
SetFileReadIgnorePatterns exists, but rg shows only tests call it in the current codebase.
Orphaned plugin-cache exclusion helpers exist, but rg found no production setup call.

gaps.impact: Permission/robustness parity gap: Grep can enumerate or match files TS would hide, and large searches may return different first-page results after denied files are included.

gaps.title: Structured output data and exact model-facing text do not match TS
gaps.description: TS Grep returns a structured data object with mode, numFiles, filenames, content, numLines, numMatches, appliedLimit, and appliedOffset, then maps that object to exact tool_result text per output mode. Go Grep returns plain newline-joined text plus string metadata. It does not emit the TS data shape, lacks the exact 'Found N files' and count-mode summary text, uses punctuation-different empty messages, omits appliedLimit/appliedOffset in model-visible text, and does not set Grep's 20K maxResultSizeChars persistence threshold.

ts_evidence.note: TS outputSchema defines mode, numFiles, filenames, content, numLines, numMatches, appliedLimit, and appliedOffset.
TS mapToolResultToToolResultBlockParam renders content/count/files modes with exact pagination, count summary, and 'Found N file(s)' text.
TS call returns structured data for content, count, and files_with_matches modes.
TS sets maxResultSizeChars to 20,000 for Grep.

go_evidence.note: Go ToolResult has string Content, optional ContentBlocks, IsError, and string Metadata rather than a typed Grep output object.
Go Grep records output_mode/truncated/match_count/num_matches/multiline/duration_ms metadata and returns plain text ContentBlocks.
Go empty messages are 'No files found.' or 'No matches found.' with periods, unlike TS model text.
Go can honor maxResultSizeChars metadata, but Grep does not set the TS 20K per-tool threshold.

gaps.impact: Downstream consumers and the model see different payloads, summaries, empty states, pagination hints, count metadata, and large-result persistence behavior.

gaps.title: files_with_matches ordering is opposite the TS mtime sort
gaps.description: For default files_with_matches mode, TS stats all matching files and sorts newest-first by modification time, with filename tiebreaking (and filename-only sorting in NODE_ENV=test). Go's ripgrep path adds --sort=modified for directories and then explicitly sorts results with lower mtime first before applying pagination at Execute. This changes which files appear first and which files survive head_limit/offset.

ts_evidence.note: TS stats all results, sorts by b[1] - a[1] (newest first), then applies head_limit/offset and relativizes.

go_evidence.note: Go adds --sort=modified for files_with_matches directory searches.
Go sorts directory results with searchResultModTime(i) < searchResultModTime(j), i.e. oldest first, before relativizing.
Execute applies head_limit after runGrepWithRipgrep returns the already sorted result slice.
The fallback path sorts files newest-first, so native rg and fallback can disagree with each other.

gaps.impact: Default Grep may prioritize stale files over recent ones and paginate a different result set than TS.

gaps.title: Actual ripgrep execution bypasses the TS-equivalent locator/config path
gaps.description: TS centralizes ripgrep selection: system rg only when requested, embedded mode via argv0 with --no-config, vendored builtin fallback, first-use version testing, codesign/quarantine handling on macOS, timeout, EAGAIN retry, and partial-result behavior. Go has a richer LocateRipgrep implementation, but runRipgrep still calls a separate resolveRipgrepPath that only does exec.LookPath('rg'). It ignores CLAUDE_RG_PATH, embedded/bundled paths, version verification, codesign setup, and USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP-style semantics. When rg is missing, Go also silently falls back to a Go regexp scanner whose ignore/regex/multiline semantics are not TS ripgrep.

ts_evidence.note: TS chooses system, embedded, or builtin ripgrep and adds --no-config for embedded mode.
TS ripGrepRaw uses ripgrepCommand's command/args/argv0 for each call.
TS codesigns if needed and tests ripgrep on first use.
TS caches ripgrep status after a --version sanity check.
TS handles macOS codesign and quarantine for the builtin rg binary.

go_evidence.note: Go LocateRipgrep supports override, PATH, embedded fallback, and --version verification.
The richer locator knows CLAUDE_RG_PATH and embedded paths.
resolveRipgrepPath uses only exec.LookPath('rg') and a separate cache.
runRipgrep calls resolveRipgrepPath, not LocateRipgrep.
runGrepWithRipgrep falls back to runGrepWithFallback on ripgrep unavailable.
Fallback uses Go regexp/file walking rather than TS's bundled/builtin ripgrep execution path.

gaps.impact: Runtime behavior depends on the host PATH and can silently drift from TS rg semantics, especially in bundled distributions, macOS quarantine cases, CI containers, and fallback mode.

gaps.title: Strict schema, semantic coercion, and pattern preservation differ from TS
gaps.description: TS uses z.strictObject and semanticNumber/semanticBoolean: unknown keys are rejected, quoted numeric/boolean literals are tolerated for numeric/boolean fields, and the search pattern is passed exactly as supplied. Go's JSONSchema cannot express additionalProperties:false, json.Unmarshal ignores unknown fields, the GrepInput struct accepts non-TS internal field names such as case_insensitive/show_line_numbers/context_before, quoted booleans/numbers fail parse, output_mode/type/glob/pattern are trimmed, and glob values starting with '-' are rejected even though TS forwards them as --glob values.

ts_evidence.note: TS input schema is z.strictObject and uses semanticNumber/semanticBoolean for Grep's numeric/boolean knobs.
TS accepts numeric string literals such as '30' and '-5'.
TS accepts only 'true'/'false' string booleans as a hidden coercion.
TS preserves pattern text and forwards each glob pattern as a --glob argument without trimming/rejecting leading '-'.

go_evidence.note: Go JSONSchema lacks additionalProperties or strict-object support.
parseInput uses json.Unmarshal into structs, which ignores unknown fields and rejects quoted bool/number values.
GrepInput exposes internal JSON names not present in TS Grep's model schema.
Go trims pattern/output_mode for validation.
Go rejects glob values beginning with '-', a stricter behavior than the TS code path.
Go passes strings.TrimSpace(in.Pattern), strings.TrimSpace(in.Type), and a trimmed glob into execution.

gaps.impact: Some TS-accepted calls fail in Go, some TS-rejected calls are accepted in Go, and whitespace-sensitive regex searches can produce wrong results.

gaps.title: Context flag precedence and edge values are not TS-compatible
gaps.description: TS treats context and -C as aliases with defined-precedence semantics: context wins whenever it is present, then -C, otherwise -B/-A. Values are passed to ripgrep whenever the key is defined, including zero and invalid/negative values that ripgrep may reject. Go collapses context/-C into a single Context float and only applies it when greater than zero; ContextBefore/ContextAfter are only emitted when greater than zero. This silently changes calls such as context:0 with -A/-B present, -C:0, negative values, and other edge cases.

ts_evidence.note: TS uses `context !== undefined`, then `context_c !== undefined`, then -B/-A checks against undefined.

go_evidence.note: Go applies context only when in.Context > 0.
Go emits -B/-A only when ContextBefore/ContextAfter are greater than zero.
Go aliases -C and context into the same field before precedence can be represented exactly.
A helper claims TS ignores context outside content mode and rejects it in Go, but this helper is only used by tests, not Execute.

gaps.impact: Edge-case context searches can return different match windows or silently succeed where TS/ripgrep would receive and potentially reject the supplied flags.

gaps.title: Timeout, cancellation, and stdout-cap partial-result behavior differs from TS
gaps.description: TS ripGrep returns partial complete lines when a timeout or buffer overflow produced output, and only rejects no-output timeouts with a descriptive RipgrepTimeoutError. Go runRipgrep can capture partial stdout on context timeout, but GrepTool.Execute always returns an IsError timeout result even when partials exist. Go's cappedBuffer also drops stdout after 50MB without surfacing that dropped state to Grep, while TS handles maxBuffer overflow as a partial-result condition.

ts_evidence.note: TS computes partial lines for non-exit-code errors, drops incomplete tail on timeout/buffer overflow, rejects only empty timeouts, and otherwise resolves lines.
TS explicitly treats ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER as partial-output overflow.
TS timeout with no results throws a descriptive RipgrepTimeoutError.

go_evidence.note: Go RipgrepTimeoutError carries Partial results.
runRipgrep returns RipgrepTimeoutError with partial stdout when ctx.Err() is set.
GrepTool.Execute renders any RipgrepTimeoutError as IsError, even with partial results.
cappedBuffer records dropped bytes, but runRipgrep returns only []string/error and Grep metadata does not expose stdout cap overflow.

gaps.impact: Slow or huge searches can be reported as errors or silently clipped where TS would give usable partial results and clearer retry guidance.

gaps.title: Grep cwd/default path and display paths are process-global instead of scoped
gaps.description: TS getCwd is async-context scoped and AgentTool uses runWithCwdOverride for explicit cwd/worktree execution, so Grep's default path and relative output follow the current agent/session context. Go Grep defaults to os.Getwd and formatSearchDisplayPath relativizes against os.Getwd. RegistryDeps.UpdateSessionContext updates RuntimeScope, plan state, background tasks, todo, cron, shell cwd, and file-tool allowed dirs, but not Grep cwd state. This can diverge during session switching, worktree isolation, or concurrent agent execution.

ts_evidence.note: TS getCwd uses AsyncLocalStorage overrides before falling back to process cwd.
GrepTool.getPath defaults to getCwd when no path is supplied.
AgentTool wraps agent execution in runWithCwdOverride for cwd/worktree contexts.
Resumed worktree agents also restore cwd via runWithCwdOverride.

go_evidence.note: resolveGrepSearchPath defaults omitted path to os.Getwd.
formatSearchDisplayPath relativizes output against os.Getwd.
UpdateSessionContext has no Grep/Glob cwd or scope state to update.
GrepTool is an empty struct, so it cannot carry per-session cwd state.

gaps.impact: Default searches and relative result paths may point at the wrong root in nontrivial runtime contexts.

gaps.title: Type-filter validation and usage-error semantics are Go-specific
gaps.description: TS does not prevalidate the type parameter; it forwards --type to ripgrep and lets ripgrep's usage/error behavior flow through ripGrep. Go shells out to rg --type-list through LocateRipgrep, caches known type names, and rejects unknown values before the actual search with Go-generated suggestion text. This is useful but not exact: it can reject before TS would run rg, it uses a different rg locator than the actual search path, and fallback mode can accept values with only a simplified extension map.

ts_evidence.note: TS simply appends --type and the provided type value.
TS ripGrep handles ripgrep exit codes/errors after execution; there is no Grep-specific --type-list validation.

go_evidence.note: Go prevalidates non-empty type values with ValidateGrepType before running search.
ValidateGrepType rejects unknown types and formats Go-specific suggestions/errors.
Type discovery uses LocateRipgrep and rg --type-list, which differs from runRipgrep's current resolveRipgrepPath execution path.
Fallback mode maps types through a simplified extension switch, not ripgrep's full type definitions.

gaps.impact: Invalid or uncommon type filters produce different errors and may have different behavior depending on whether the rg or fallback path is used.

gaps.title: Tool description, discovery metadata, and UI/rendering hooks are incomplete
gaps.description: TS Grep's prompt is a rich instruction block that tells the model to prefer Grep over Bash grep/rg, documents ripgrep regex, filters, output modes, Agent escalation, brace escaping, and multiline behavior. The tool also exposes searchHint, userFacingName, activity description, render hooks, extractSearchText, read-only/search classification, and concurrency metadata. Go Grep's Description is a short sentence and the Tool interface/registry metadata do not represent most of those affordances.

ts_evidence.note: TS prompt provides detailed model-facing guidance and usage constraints.
TS declares searchHint, maxResultSizeChars, user-facing name, activity description, read-only/concurrency, classifier, and search/read command classification.
TS wires render hooks and extractSearchText for search-result summarization.
TS UI summarizes line/file/match counts by output mode.

go_evidence.note: Go Description is only a short one-line capability summary.
Go Tool interface lacks read-only/search classifier/render hook methods.
Builtin discovery metadata does not include a Grep searchHint entry.
Go provides metadata/text blocks but no TS-equivalent render summary contract.

gaps.impact: The model and UI receive weaker guidance and less structured search summarization than TS, even when raw search results are correct.

gaps.title: Grep parity tests miss key runtime gaps and current package verification is blocked
gaps.description: Go has many direct Grep tests for output modes, fallback behavior, head_limit, hidden/VCS handling, dashed patterns, metadata, and type/filter helpers. However, the current tests do not cover SetupRegistry/UpdateSessionContext wiring, file-read deny/plugin cache exclusions, TS exact model text, newest-first files_with_matches ordering, rg locator/embedded override behavior, strict unknown-key rejection, semantic quoted booleans/numbers, whitespace-preserving patterns, context:0 precedence, timeout partial success, or single-file count-mode structured summary parity. A focused `go test ./tools -run 'TestGrep' -count=1` currently fails to build due unrelated MCP compile errors before Grep tests run.

ts_evidence.note: TS input schema provides edge cases that need fixture coverage.
TS exact model-facing output text needs tests.
TS permission ignore/plugin exclusions need runtime tests.
TS ripgrep selection behavior needs locator/config tests.

go_evidence.note: The file header is stale: it still says each case must fail against current production code, but several covered gaps have been implemented.
Conformance tests focus heavily on direct Execute fallback behavior and do not exercise registry/runtime wiring.
Search tests cover basic Grep behavior but not the remaining TS exact-output/permission/locator edge cases.
Current focused tools-package verification fails on undefined MCP helpers before Grep tests run.
Current tools-package verification also fails on firstNonEmpty redeclaration.
Current tools-package verification also fails on conn.client.GetInstructions being undefined.

gaps.impact: Existing tests can pass or fail for reasons unrelated to Grep while leaving high-risk parity gaps unverified.
